content.comment_body: Hello, I've created a control program for two pumps running and two pumps on standby, but I'm experiencing an issue: when I activate the input for the next duty cycle, one of the previously running pumps briefly turns ON and OFF (almost instantly). I'm unable to identify the cause. I've observed this behavior consistently during tests with [product_name] software, but when examining the physical hardware (LEDs), this issue doesn't happen in every cycle and sometimes doesn't occur at all. What might be causing this? Any advice would be appreciated.

This issue seems to be caused by the way the program is written. A straightforward solution is to add On-Delay Timers with a short delay to the relay outputs. If you share your program, we can review it and possibly find the root of the problem.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing inconsistent and brief relay activations in their pump control program, particularly when using [product_name] software. The ON/OFF cycling is not always present on the actual hardware, creating uncertainty between simulation and real-world behavior. This illustrates challenges in troubleshooting and debugging automation logic when there is a mismatch between software and hardware performance.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the pump control logic to run smoothly without unintended short ON/OFF actions, and for software simulation results to accurately reflect those seen in the physical hardware.
